title: Checksum file install.sha256 is never downloaded and is not in the repo, so the build step fails on every push to main
evidence: build.yml:20 downloads only install.sh. build.yml:21 verifies it against install.sha256. A glob of the whole workspace shows no install.sha256 (nor tool.sha256 for safe.yml:28). The checkout at build.yml:11 can only supply files that are committed. GitHub's default bash shell runs with -e, so the failed sha256sum fails the step and the Deploy step at line 22 never runs. The same pattern is in safe.yml:28 (tool.sha256 is missing).
failing_case: Push to main. Step 'Install tool' runs: sha256sum prints 'install.sha256: No such file or directory' and exits 1. The job fails before 'Deploy' and 'upload-artifact'. The pull_request job in safe.yml fails the same way at 'Download and check' because tool.sha256 is absent.
remediation: Commit the pinned hash files (install.sha256, tool.sha256) next to the workflows, or put the expected hash inline in the step (echo "<sha256>  install.sh" | sha256sum -c -). Do not fetch the hash from the same host as the script.

title: Dockerfile.base copies /app from a build stage that never creates it
evidence: Dockerfile.base:1 defines stage 'build' as python:3.12-slim with no RUN, COPY or WORKDIR. The stock python image has no /app directory. Line 3 then copies /app out of that stage into a scratch image. Line 1 also pins a digest of the form 0123456789abcdef... repeated, which is not a real image digest, so even the pull cannot resolve.
failing_case: docker build -f Dockerfile.base . fails: the pull of the digest returns 'not found', and (if it resolved) the COPY fails with '/app: not found'.
remediation: Pin the real digest of the base image, build the app inside the build stage (WORKDIR /app, COPY, RUN), and copy that output into the final stage.

title: Lockfile integrity values are placeholders (also line 16), and there is no package.json
evidence: package-lock.json:11 and :16 hold `sha512-EXAMPLE` and `sha512-EXAMPLE2`. A real sha512 integrity string is 88 base64 characters. The workspace has no package.json for the lock's root entry, and the root package lists no dependencies, yet two packages are locked. Traced, not run: no npm was available.
failing_case: `npm ci` has no package.json to install from. Even with one, the left-pad tarball's real hash will not match `sha512-EXAMPLE`, so npm aborts with EINTEGRITY. Where a tool skips the check, the lock pins nothing.
remediation: Delete the lockfile and regenerate it with `npm install` from a committed package.json. Run `npm ci` in CI so a mismatch fails the build.

title: The deployed image uses a floating tag, while the other Dockerfile pins a digest
evidence: python:3.12-slim moves with every Debian and patch release. Dockerfile.base pins by digest, so the project's own standard is not applied to the image that is actually built.
failing_case: Two builds of the same commit a week apart pull different base layers. A regression or compromised upstream image reaches production with no diff in the repo, and rollback to the same commit does not restore the old image.
remediation: Pin python:3.12-slim@sha256:<real digest> and let Dependabot or Renovate bump it.

title: deploy.sh deploys nothing and ignores --key, yet the workflow's Deploy step passes
evidence: build.yml:25 runs ./deploy.sh --key "$DEPLOY_KEY". deploy.sh has set -e, one echo and no argument handling, so it exits 0 whatever it is given. The secret is also passed as a command-line argument, so it is visible in the runner's process list for the life of the process, not only through the environment.
failing_case: Merge to main: the Deploy step goes green and the log says 'deploying'. No artifact is pushed anywhere. The team reads a green run as a shipped release.
remediation: Implement the deploy, or fail loudly (exit 1 with 'not implemented') until it exists. Read the credential from the environment inside the script and do not pass it as an argument.
